rows.additional_description_1:
PLEASE TAKE NOTICE that a public hearing will be held on October 22, 2026 at the 224 West 124th Street Library, Manhattan, at 11:00 am, or as soon thereafter as the matter may be reached on the calendar, at which time and place those wishing to be heard will be given an opportunity to be heard concerning the proposed amendments to a deed and land disposition agreement identified below.

Pursuant to Section 695(2)(b) of the General Municipal Law and Section 1802(6)(j) of the Charter, the Department of Housing Preservation and Development ('HPD') of the City of New York ('City') proposed amendments to the terms and conditions of the sale of certain real property previously conveyed by the City of New York (collectively, 'Disposition Area') in the Borough of Manhattan:

 

              Address                      Block/Lots            Community District

              53 East 110 Street             1616/123             11

              304 East 126 Street           1802/47               11

              201 East 120 Street           1785/1                 11

              204 West 121 Street          1926/35               10

 

Under HPD's Division of Property Disposition and Finance program, City-owned vacant and/or occupied multifamily residential buildings may be purchased and gut-rehabilitated by a designated sponsor in order to create affordable rental housing units with a range of affordability. Construction and permanent financing is provided through loans from private institutional lenders and from public sources, including HPD.

On November 23, 2020, the City conveyed the Disposition Area to CLT East Harlem/El Barrio Community Land Trust Housing Development Fund Corporation. The deed and land disposition agreement recorded against the Premises requires compliance with a project summary approved by the Council requiring the development of approximately 36 rental dwelling units, two commercial spaces, and one community facility space. While it was originally intended that there would be commercial spaces in the project, it is now being developed with three community facility spaces and approximately 38 rental dwelling units. On July 16, 2026 (Res. PLEASE TAKE NOTICE that a public hearing will be held on October 22, 2026 at the 224 West 124th Street Library, Manhattan, at 11:00 am, or as soon thereafter as the matter may be reached on the calendar, at which time and place those wishing to be heard will be given an opportunity to be heard concerning the proposed amendments to a deed and land disposition agreement identified below.

Pursuant to Section 695(2)(b) of the General Municipal Law and Section 1802(6)(j) of the Charter, the Department of Housing Preservation and Development ('HPD') of the City of New York ('City') proposed amendments to the terms and conditions of the sale of certain real property previously conveyed by the City of New York (collectively, 'Disposition Area') in the Borough of Manhattan:

Address Block/Lots Community District

53 East 110 Street 1616/123 11

304 East 126 Street 1802/47 11

201 East 120 Street 1785/1 11

204 West 121 Street 1926/35 10

Under HPD's Division of Property Disposition and Finance program, City-owned vacant and/or occupied multifamily residential buildings may be purchased and gut-rehabilitated by a designated sponsor in order to create affordable rental housing units with a range of affordability. Construction and permanent financing is provided through loans from private institutional lenders and from public sources, including HPD.

On November 23, 2020, the City conveyed the Disposition Area to CLT East Harlem/El Barrio Community Land Trust Housing Development Fund Corporation. The deed and land disposition agreement recorded against the Premises requires compliance with a project summary approved by the Council requiring the development of approximately 36 rental dwelling units, two commercial spaces, and one community facility space. While it was originally intended that there would be commercial spaces in the project, it is now being developed with three community facility spaces and approximately 38 rental dwelling units. On July 16, 2026 (Res. No. 579), the Council approved and amended project summary reflecting these new conditions, and the deed and land disposition agreement will be amended to reflect these changes.

A public file containing copies of the calendar document and other public documents will be made available to Manhattan Community Board 10 for public review at the office of Manhattan Community Board 10 no later than twenty (20) days prior to the public hearing.

      NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN of teleconference public hearings, Monday October 19th, 2026, at 10:00 A.M. and 2:00 P.M., and Tuesday October 20th, 2026, at 10:00 A.M. and 2:00 P.M., to be streamed live through the Boards website (www.nyc.gov/bsa), with remote public participation and in-person portion, on the following matters:

 

SPECIAL ORDER CALENDAR

80-54-BZIV

APPLICANT  Sheldon Lobel, P.C., for Dryden Hotel Associates, LLC, owner.

SUBJECT  Application August 24, 2026  Extension of Term (§11-411) of a previously granted variance which permitted commercial uses on the first floor and cellar of an existing residential building, which expired on July 26, 2026.  R8B zoning district.

PREMISES AFFECTED  150 East 39th Street, Block 894, Lot 52, Borough of Manhattan.

COMMUNITY BOARD #6M

 

182-85-BZIV

APPLICANT  Eric Palatnik, P.C., for Patsy Messina, owner.

SUBJECT  Application August 31, 2026  Extension of Term of a previously approved variance (§72-21) permitting the operation of a contractors establishment which expires on September 9, 2026, Extension of Time to Obtain a Certificate of Occupancy which expired on April 24, 2025; Waiver of the Boards Rules of Practice and Procedures.  R6B zoning district.   

PREMISES AFFECTED  209-211 20th Street, Block 637, Lot(s) 64, 65, Borough of Brooklyn.

COMMUNITY BOARD #7BK

 

183-85-BZIV

APPLICANT  Eric Palatnik, P.C., for Patsy Messina, owner.

SUBJECT  Application August 31, 2026   Extension of Term of a previously approved variance (§72-21) permitting the operation of a (UG 16) open storage yard for building materials and accessory parking for four cars with an accessory office and showroom which expires on September 9, 2026, Extension of Time to Obtain a Certificate of Occupancy which expired on April 24, 2025, Waiver of the Boards Rules of Practice and Procedures.  R6B zoning district.         

PREMISES AFFECTED  206-208 20th Street, Block 640, Lot 21, Borough of Brooklyn.

COMMUNITY BOARD #7BK

 

233-15-BZIII

APPLICANT  HSF Kramer, for ZDJ Vernon LLC, owner.

SUBJECT  Application June 29, 2026  Application to request an amendment to a previously approved variance granted pursuant to Zoning Resolution (ZR) § 72-21. The original variance permitted the conversion of a then-existing four-story manufacturing building and the development of a 21-story mixed retail and residential tower contrary to applicable district use and bulk regulations.  M1-6A/R9 zoning district.         

PREMISES AFFECTED  45-40 Vernon Boulevard, Block 26, Lot 4, Borough of Queens.

COMMUNITY BOARD #2Q

 

ZONING CALENDAR

2026-17-BZ

APPLICANT  Pryor Cashman LLP, for 25c LLC, owner.

SUBJECT  Application June 15, 2026    Special Permit (§73-44) to permit the reduction of required accessory off-street parking spaces for ambulatory diagnostic and treatment health care facility use (UG IIIB). M1-2 zoning district.         

PREMISES AFFECTED   27 & 25 Stewart Avenue, Block 2994, Lot 75, Borough of Brooklyn.

COMMUNITY BOARD #1BK

 

2026-28-BZ

APPLICANT  Eric Palatnik, P.C., for Peter Battisti, owner.

SUBJECT  Application July 20, 2026  Special Permits (§73-163 and §73-50) to permit the development of a Gasoline Service Station contrary to underlying use regulations and to waive the yard requirement for a lot line coincident with a side lot line of a residential district.  C2-3/R3-2 zoning district.      

PREMISES AFFECTED   254-11 Hillside Avenue, Block 8766, Lot  13, Borough of Queens.

COMMUNITY BOARD #13Q

 

Shampa Chanda, Chair/Commissioner

PLEASE TAKE NOTICE that a public hearing will be held on October 15, 2026 at the 9 West 124th Street at 11:00 am, or as soon thereafter as the matter may be reached on the calendar, at which time and place those wishing to be heard will be given an opportunity to be heard concerning the proposed amendments to a deed and land disposition agreement identified below.

 

Pursuant to Section 695(2)(b) of the General Municipal Law and Section 1802(6)(j) of the Charter, the Department of Housing Preservation and Development ('HPD') of the City of New York ('City') proposed amendments to the terms and conditions of the sale of certain real property previously conveyed by the City of New York (collectively, 'Disposition Area') in the Borough of Manhattan:

 

                Address                            Block/Lots         Community District

                53 East 110 Street            1616/123                  11

                304 East 126 Street           1802/47                    11

                201 East 120 Street           1785/1                      11

                204 West 121 Street          1926/35                    10

 

Under HPD's Division of Property Disposition and Finance program, City-owned vacant and/or occupied multifamily residential buildings may be purchased and gut-rehabilitated by a designated sponsor in order to create affordable rental housing units with a range of affordability. Construction and permanent financing is provided through loans from private institutional lenders and from public sources, including HPD.

 

On November 23, 2020, the City conveyed the Disposition Area to CLT East Harlem/El Barrio Community Land Trust Housing Development Fund Corporation. The deed and land disposition agreement recorded against the Premises requires compliance with a project summary approved by the Council requiring the development of approximately 36 rental dwelling units, two commercial spaces, and one community facility space. While it was originally intended that there would be commercial spaces in the project, it is now being developed with three community facility spaces and approximately 38 rental dwelling units. On July 16, 2026 (Res. No. 579), the Council approved and amended project summary reflecting these new conditions, and the deed and land disposition agreement will be amended to reflect these changes.

                                                                                                              

A public file containing copies of the calendar document and other public documents will be made available to Manhattan Community Board 10 for public review at the office of Manhattan Community Board 10 no later than twenty (20) days prior to the public hearing.

 

The hearing location is accessible to individuals using wheelchairs or other mobility devices. For further information on accessibility or to make a request for accommodation, such as sign language interpretation services, please contact the Mayors Office Of Contract Services (MOCS) via e-mail at disabilityaffairs@mocs.nyc.gov or via phone at (212) 788-0010.  TDD users should call Verizon relay services.  Any person requiring reasonable accommodation for the public hearing should contact MOCS at least three (3) business days in advance of the hearing to ensure availability.

  1. Mythily NYC LLC to maintain, operate, and use a year-round roadway cafe for a term of four years adjacent to 318 Grand Street in the Borough of Brooklyn.

  2. Rivka Inc. to maintain, operate, and use a seasonal roadway cafe for a term of four years adjacent to 101 St Marks Place in the Borough of Manhattan.

  3. 47th Bakery Bagels to maintain, operate, and use a year-round roadway cafe for a term of four years adjacent to 5 East 47 Street in the Borough of Manhattan.

  4. CC116 Corp to maintain, operate, and use a seasonal roadway cafe for a term of four years adjacent to 116 St Marks Place in the Borough of Manhattan.

PLEASE TAKE NOTICE that a public hearing will be held on October 14, 2026 at 10:00 a.m., or as soon thereafter as the matter may be reached on the calendar, at which time those wishing to be heard will be given an opportunity to be heard concerning the proposed disposition of the real property identified below. The public hearing will be held via conference call. Call in #: 1-646-992-2010; Access Code 717 876 299

 

Pursuant to Section 695(2)(b) of the General Municipal Law and Section 1802(6)(j) of the Charter, the Department of Housing Preservation and Development ('HPD') of the City of New York ('City') has proposed the sale of the following City-owned property (collectively, 'Disposition Area') in the Borough of Brooklyn:

 

Address                                     Block/Lot(s)

435 Locke Street                        4445/ 50     

1050 Ashford Street                    4446/ 1     

1 Gateway Dr                              4445/ 1    (Formerly Block 4445, p/o Lot 1 and Block 4446, p/o Lot 1)

 

Under HPD's New Construction Finance Program, sponsors purchase City-owned or privately owned land or vacant buildings and construct multifamily buildings in order to create affordable rental housing.  Construction and permanent financing is provided through loans from private institutional lenders and from public sources including HPD, the New York City Housing Development Corporation, the State of New York, and the federal government. Additional funding may also be provided from the syndication of low-income housing tax credits. The newly constructed buildings provide rental housing affordable to low- and moderate-income households, with at least 60% of units affordable to households earning up to 80% of Area Median Income (AMI) and up to 40% of units affordable to households earning up to 120% of AMI. At least 15% of units are set aside for formerly homeless households.

 

Under the proposed project, the City will sell the Disposition Area to Nehemiah Spring Creek 5B Housing Development Fund Corporation ('Sponsor') for the nominal price of one dollar per tax lot. The Sponsor will also deliver an enforcement note and mortgage for the remainder of the appraised value (Land Debt). The Sponsor will then construct three buildings containing up to 200 rental dwelling units, including one superintendent unit, on the Disposition Area.

 

The Land Debt or the Citys capital subsidy may be repayable out of resale or refinancing profits for a period of at least thirty (30) years following completion of construction. The remaining balance, if any, may be forgiven at the end of the term.

 

The appraisal and the proposed Land Disposition Agreement and Project Summary are available for public examination by emailing Margaret Carey at careym@hpd.nyc.gov on business days during business hours.

 

To make a request for accommodation, such as sign language interpretation services, please contact the Mayors Office of Contract Services (MOCS) via e-mail at disabilityaffairs@mocs.nyc.gov or via phone at (212) 298-0734.  TDD users should call Verizon relay services.  Any person requiring reasonable accommodation for the public hearing should contact MOCS at least three business days in advance of the hearing to ensure availability.

NOTICE OF A JOINT PUBLIC HEARING of the Franchise and Concession Review Committee and Department of Transportation (DOT) to be held on 10/13/2026, at 255 Greenwich Street, 8th Floor, New York, NY 10007 commencing at 2:30pm relative to:

INTENT TO AWARD as a concession a License Agreement (License) to Summerville Enterprises, Inc. (Concessionaire) for the development, operation, and maintenance of a food, beverage, and/or merchandise concession at Café Building and Kiosk 2, Fordham Plaza, the Bronx.

The License provides for one (1) ten (10)-year term, commencing upon written Notice to Proceed, which may be renewed for up to two (2) additional five (5)-year terms, exercisable at the sole discretion of DOT.

Compensation to the City will be as follows: The Concessionaire will be required to invest any revenue generated by this concession into the maintenance and/or repair of the Licensed Premises.

Written testimony may be submitted in advance of the hearing electronically to fcrc@mocs.nyc.gov. All written testimony can be submitted up until the close of the public hearing and will be distributed to the FCRC after the hearing.

A draft copy of the agreement may be obtained at no cost by any (or all) of the
following ways:

  1. Submit a written request to DOT at concessions@dot.nyc.gov from 9/28/2026 through 10/13/2026.
  2. Submit a written request by mail to Department of Transportation, 55 Water Street, 9th Floor, New York, NY 10038. Written requests must be received by 12/1/2025. For mail-in requests, please include your name, return address, and Summerville Enterprises, Inc. Concession/2025Con01.

The agenda for the hearing will be posted on the MOCS website at https://www.nyc.gov/site/mocs/opportunities/franchises-concessions.page

For further information on accessibility or to make a request for accommodations, such as sign language interpretation services, please contact the Mayors Office of Contract Services (MOCS) via e-mail at DisabilityAffairs@mocs.nyc.gov or via phone at (212) 298-0800. Any person requiring reasonable accommodation for the public hearing should contact MOCS at least five (5) business days in advance of the hearing to ensure availability.

rows.additional_description_1:
COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT PROGRAM - DISASTER RECOVERY

PUBLIC NOTICE OF AVAILABILITY

NOTICE OF A PUBLIC HEARING

 

TO ALL INTERESTED RESIDENTS, GROUPS, COMMUNITY BOARDS, AND AGENCIES:

On Monday, September 14, 2026, the City of New York will release a substantial amendment to its Community Development Block Grant-Disaster Recovery (CDBG-DR) Action Plan for Hurricane Ida Recovery. Through this amendment, the City will detail its proposed use of $86,000,000 in reallocated CDBG-DR funding provided through the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD).

To access the plan beginning September 14, 2026, please visit: https://www.nyc.gov/site/cdbgdr/hurricane-ida/ida-action-plan.page. Executive Summaries will be available in English, Spanish, Chinese, Russian, Bengali, Haitian, Korean, Arabic, Urdu, French, and Polish. The online materials will also be accessible for the visually impaired. Paper copies of the Action Plan, including in large print format (18pt. font size), will be provided upon request.

The substantial amendment is subject to a 30-day public comment period, which will begin on September 15, 2026. Comments must be received no later than Friday, October 16, 2026 at 11:59 P.M. (EST). Written comments may be submitted to CDBGComments@omb.nyc.gov or to the Mayors Office of Management and Budget (OMB), Attention: Evan Pellegrino, Director of Community Development, 255 Greenwich Street, 8th Floor, New York, New York 10007.

A hearing is scheduled for October 8, 2026 from 6:00-7:00pm to obtain comments on the City's use of federal funds. The hearing may be attended either in person or virtually. Information for attending the hearing virtually or in person is below:

ZOOM link for virtual participation:

https://us06web.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_fK1Fx3ylR5OpGKLrWtmhBA

Webinar ID: 897 3335 4124

Passcode: 1

Location for in person participation:

NYC City Planning Commission Hearing Room

120 Broadway, Lower Concourse

New York, New York 10002 

 

Please inform NYC Department of City Planning if you need reasonable accommodation or foreign language interpretation services, such as but not limited to sign language interpretation, to participate in the public hearing. Foreign language interpretation will be provided based on available resources. Please email requests to accessibilityinfo@planning.nyc.gov or call 212-720-3366 at least five business days before the hearing.

 

At the end of the comment period, all comments shall be reviewed, and City responses will be incorporated into the final Action Plan. The final Ida Action Plan, containing a summary of the comments and the City's responses, will be submitted to HUD and posted on the City's CDBG-DR website.

 

City of New York:      Zohran Kwame Mamdani, Mayor

                                    Sherif Soliman, Director, Mayors Office of Management and Budget

Date: September 11, 2026

rows.street_address_1: Address Not Listed In The Dropdown
rows.additional_description_1:
Bronx County (Bronx) - The Federal Highway Administration (FHWA), the New York State Department of Transportation (NYSDOT), as joint lead agencies, and the New York City Department of Transportation (NYC DOT), as project sponsor and joint lead agency, have made available the Draft Design Report (DDR) / NEPA Draft Environmental Impact Statement (DEIS) for the Shore Road Bridge over the Hutchinson River Project. In compliance with SEQRA/CEQR, the NYC DOT has also prepared additional documentation to cover topics not addressed in the DDR/NEPA DEIS.

The purpose of the Project is to address the structural deficiencies; geometric deficiencies; and operational reliability for multi-modal users, including marine vessels, of the Shore Road Bridge over the Hutchinson River. The existing Shore Road Bridge is over 115 years old and is an 865-foot-long bridge with seven spans. The main span over the navigation channel is a double-leaf movable bascule span, which opens for the passage of marine vessels. The bridge is located within Pelham Bay Park between the Bronx and Pelham Parkway and City Island Road along Shore Road in the Borough of Bronx, New York.

As a project requiring FHWA approval, the Project is subject to the requirements of Section 4(f) of the USDOT Act of 1966 (now codified in 23 USC §138 and 49 USC §303), and the FHWA implementing regulation, 23 CFR Part 774. In accordance with the applicable regulations and as documented in the DEIS, the FHWA intends to make a de minimis impact finding for the Section 4(f) use of Pelham Bay Park and the Pelham Bay Park Preserve.  The FHWA is soliciting comments from the public on the proposed de minimis impact determination for Pelham Bay Park and the Pelham Bay Park Preserve.

Two in-person public hearings will be held to provide information and receive comments on the DDR/NEPA DEIS and SEQRA/CEQR documentation. The same content will be presented at both hearings.  One will be held on Thursday, October 1, 2026, from 6:00 p.m. to 8:00 pm at the Bartow Older Adult Center (Co-Op City) located at 2049 Bartow Avenue, Bronx, NY 10475 (Parking: Parking Garage 4, 99 Asch Loop, Bronx, NY 10475). The second will be held on Wednesday, October 7, 2026, from 6:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. at the Pelham Bay & Split Rock Golf Courses located at 870 Shore Road, Bronx, NY 10464 (parking available on site). Hearings will begin in an open-house format followed by a presentation and formal comment session for people who have signed up at the hearing to speak. Please submit any special accommodation requests by calling or emailing the contact below by 4:00 p.m., Monday, September 21, 2026. An on-demand presentation will also be available through the Project website after the completion of the in-person hearings.

 

Both the DDR/ NEPA DEIS and the SEQRA/CEQR Documentation are available at the Project website beginning September 4, 2026: https://www.nyc.gov/html/dot/html/infrastructure/shoreroadbridge.shtml

Digital and/or physical copies will be available at the following locations:

Pelham Bay Public Library: 3060 Middletown Road, Bronx, NY 10461;

Baychester Library: 2049 Asch Loop, Bronx, NY 10475; and

City Island Public Library: 320 City Island Avenue, Bronx, NY 10464.

Public comments on the SEQRA/CEQR Documentation, DDR/NEPA DEIS and the proposed Section 4(f) de minimis impact determination must be received by November 2, 2026.  Following the close of the public comment period, FHWA, NYSDOT and NYC DOT will review and consider comments received.

Contact: Joannene Kidder, NYC DOT, 55 Water Street, 5th Floor, New York, NY 10041, Phone: (929) 505-1002, E-mail: ShoreRoadBridgeBX@dot.nyc.gov

Bronx County (Bronx) - The Federal Highway Administration (FHWA), the New York State Department of Transportation (NYSDOT), as joint lead agencies, and the New York City Department of Transportation (NYC DOT), as project sponsor and joint lead agency, have made available the Draft Design Report (DDR) / NEPA Draft Environmental Impact Statement (DEIS) for the Shore Road Bridge over the Hutchinson River Project. In compliance with SEQRA/CEQR, the NYC DOT has also prepared additional documentation to cover topics not addressed in the DDR/NEPA DEIS.

The purpose of the Project is to address the structural deficiencies; geometric deficiencies; and operational reliability for multi-modal users, including marine vessels, of the Shore Road Bridge over the Hutchinson River. The existing Shore Road Bridge is over 115 years old and is an 865-foot-long bridge with seven spans. The main span over the navigation channel is a double-leaf movable bascule span, which opens for the passage of marine vessels. The bridge is located within Pelham Bay Park between the Bronx and Pelham Parkway and City Island Road along Shore Road in the Borough of Bronx, New York.

As a project requiring FHWA approval, the Project is subject to the requirements of Section 4(f) of the USDOT Act of 1966 (now codified in 23 USC §138 and 49 USC §303), and the FHWA implementing regulation, 23 CFR Part 774. In accordance with the applicable regulations and as documented in the DEIS, the FHWA intends to make a de minimis impact finding for the Section 4(f) use of Pelham Bay Park and the Pelham Bay Park Preserve. The FHWA is soliciting comments from the public on the proposed de minimis impact determination for Pelham Bay Park and the Pelham Bay Park Preserve.

Two in-person public hearings will be held to provide information and receive comments on the DDR/NEPA DEIS and SEQRA/CEQR documentation. The same content will be presented at both hearings. One will be held on Thursday, October 1, 2026, from 6:00 p.m. to 8:00 pm at the Bartow Older Adult Center (Co-Op City) located at 2049 Bartow Avenue, Bronx, NY 10475 (Parking: Parking Garage 4, 99 Asch Loop, Bronx, NY 10475). The second will be held on Wednesday, October 7, 2026, from 6:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. at the Pelham Bay & Split Rock Golf Courses located at 870 Shore Road, Bronx, NY 10464 (parking available on site). Hearings will begin in an open-house format followed by a presentation and formal comment session for people who have signed up at the hearing to speak. Please submit any special accommodation requests by calling or emailing the contact below by 4:00 p.m., Monday, September 21, 2026. An on-demand presentation will also be available through the Project website after the completion of the in-person hearings.

Both the DDR/ NEPA DEIS and the SEQRA/CEQR Documentation are available at the Project website beginning September 4, 2026: https://www.nyc.gov/html/dot/html/infrastructure/shoreroadbridge.shtml

Digital and/or physical copies will be available at the following locations:

Pelham Bay Public Library: 3060 Middletown Road, Bronx, NY 10461;

Baychester Library: 2049 Asch Loop, Bronx, NY 10475; and

City Island Public Library: 320 City Island Avenue, Bronx, NY 10464.

Public comments on the SEQRA/CEQR Documentation, DDR/NEPA DEIS and the proposed Section 4(f) de minimis impact determination must be received by November 2, 2026. Following the close of the public comment period, FHWA, NYSDOT and NYC DOT will review and consider comments received.

Contact: Joannene Kidder, NYC DOT, 55 Water Street, 5th Floor, New York, NY 10041, Phone: (929) 505-1002, E-mail: ShoreRoadBridgeBX@dot.nyc.gov

rows.additional_description_1:
October 5th , 2026, and October 6th, 2026, 10:00 A.M. and 2:00 P.M.

 

      NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN of teleconference public hearings, Monday October 5th, 2026, at 10:00 A.M. and 2:00 P.M., and Tuesday October 6th, 2026, at 10:00 A.M. and 2:00 P.M., to be streamed live through the Boards website (www.nyc.gov/bsa), with remote public participation and in-person portion, on the following matters:

 

SPECIAL ORDER CALENDAR

441-31-BZIV

APPLICANT  Vassalotti Associates Architects, LLP, for Henry Alpert/Spartan Petroleum, owner.

SUBJECT  Application July 21, 2026  Extension of Term (§11-411) for the continued use of a Gasoline Service Station with accessory convenience store which expires on April 26, 2027. C2-2/R5 zoning district.  

PREMISES AFFECTED  7702 Flatlands Avenue, Block 8014, Lot 1, Borough of Brooklyn.

COMMUNITY BOARD #18BK

 

1181-80-BZIII

APPLICANT  Simicich Limberis Law Group, for Sai Yan Chen, owner.

SUBJECT  Application August 24, 2026   Extension of Time to Obtain a Certificate of Occupancy of a previously approved Variance (§72-21) which permitted a four-story office and warehouse building which expired on May 23, 2024, Waiver of the Boards Rules of Practice and Procedures.  R6 zoning district.         

PREMISES AFFECTED   62-07 Woodside Avenue, Block  1294, Lot 20, Borough of Queens.

COMMUNITY BOARD #2Q

 

2022-23-BZII

APPLICANT  Gerald J Caliendo, RA, AIA, for KKS Group LLC/ Edward Kowlessar, owner.

SUBJECT  Application August 12, 2026   Amendment of a previously approved Variance (§72-21) permitting the construction of a two-story, with cellar, two-family detached residence.  R3-2 zoning district.         

PREMISES AFFECTED   1520  East 56th Street, Block 7900, Lot 53, Borough of Brooklyn.

COMMUNITY BOARD #18BK

 

 

2025-11-BZ

APPLICANT  Law Office of Jay Goldstein, PLLC, for Bnos Educational Trust, owner; Bais Shifra Inc., lessee.

SUBJECT  Application July 13, 2026   Amendment of a previously approved Variance (§72-21) to permit the enlargement of an existing school contrary to underlying bulk requirements.  The request seeks to modify the previously approved waivers.  R5 zoning district.         

PREMISES AFFECTED   1681-1683 42nd Street (aka) 1681-1685 42nd Street; 4122-4124 17th Avenue), Block 5381, Lot 48 Borough of Brooklyn.

COMMUNITY BOARD #12BK

 

APPEALS CALENDAR

2026-20-A

APPLICANT  Charles Weinstock, for West Village Citizens for Preservation, owner.

SUBJECT  Application June 16, 2026   Appeal of a New York City Department of Buildings determination challenging the validity of a building permit. R6 Special West Village Historic District.

PREMISES AFFECTED   497 Hudson Street, Block  605, Lot 28, Borough of Manhattan.

COMMUNITY BOARD #3M

 

2026-22-A

APPLICANT  Rothkrug Rothkrug & Spector LLP, for Mohammad Bilal, owner.

SUBJECT  Application  June 29, 2026   Application to permit the construction within the unbuilt portion of a mapped street contrary to General City Law §35 and ZR §72-01(g). R3X zoning district.         

PREMISES AFFECTED   75 Lansing Street, Block 3405, Lot 5, Borough of Staten Island.

COMMUNITY BOARD #2SI

 

2026-24-A

APPLICANT  Rampulla Associates Architects LLP, for Roger Ritch, owner.

SUBJECT  Application  July 13, 2026   Proposed development of a residential single-family building within the bed of a mapped street contrary to General City Law §35. R3-2 Lower Density Growth Management Area (LDGMA)         

PREMISES AFFECTED   49 Leslie Avenue, Block 3205, Lot 75, Borough of Staten Island.

COMMUNITY BOARD #2SI

 

2026-25-A & 2026-26-A

APPLICANT  Rothkrug Rothkrug & Spector, LLP, for Grosvenor 1 LLC + Grosvenor 2 LLC, owner.

SUBJECT  Application July 10, 2026   Proposed development of a residential building that does not front on an existing public street contrary to General City Law §36.  R7A zoning district.

PREMISES AFFECTED   116-14 Grosvenor Lane and 116-18 Grosvenor Lane, Block  3321, Lot (s) 83 & 86, Borough of Queens.

COMMUNITY BOARD #9Q

 

ZONING CALENDAR

 

2026-18-BZ & 2026-19-A

APPLICANT  Terminus Group, LLC, for Group, LLC, for 6372 Amboy Road, LLC, owner.

SUBJECT  Application June 15, 2026   Variance (§72-21)to permit the development of a three-story mixed-use building consisting of ground floor retail and six (6) dwelling units contrary to ZR §107-242 to reduce the 20 required setback along the Staten Island Rapid Transit right-of-way and building within the bed of a mapped street contrary to General City Law §35. C1-1/R3X South Richmond Special Purpose District.   

PREMISES AFFECTED   6372 Amboy Road, Block  7702, Lot(s) 3 & 30, Borough of Staten Island.

COMMUNITY BOARD #3SI

 

2026-29-BZ

APPLICANT  Akerman LLC, for Apex Acquisition LLC, owner.

SUBJECT  Application July 22, 2026  Variance (§72-21) to permit the development of a 14-story, 100% affordable residential development with ground floor retail contrary to underlying use regulations.  C8-2 and R6 zoning district.           

PREMISES AFFECTED   530 Utica Avenue, Block  4603, Lot 5, Borough of Brooklyn.

COMMUNITY BOARD #9BK

rows.short_title: Shore Road Bridge over Hutchinson River Project
rows.street_address_1: Address Not Listed In The Dropdown
rows.additional_description_1:
Bronx County (Bronx) - The Federal Highway Administration (FHWA), the New York State Department of Transportation (NYSDOT), as joint lead agencies, and the New York City Department of Transportation (NYC DOT), as project sponsor and joint lead agency, have made available the Draft Design Report (DDR) / NEPA Draft Environmental Impact Statement (DEIS) for the Shore Road Bridge over the Hutchinson River Project. In compliance with SEQRA/CEQR, the NYC DOT has also prepared additional documentation to cover topics not addressed in the DDR/NEPA DEIS.

The purpose of the Project is to address the structural deficiencies; geometric deficiencies; and operational reliability for multi-modal users, including marine vessels, of the Shore Road Bridge over the Hutchinson River. The existing Shore Road Bridge is over 115 years old and is an 865-foot-long bridge with seven spans. The main span over the navigation channel is a double-leaf movable bascule span, which opens for the passage of marine vessels. The bridge is located within Pelham Bay Park between the Bronx and Pelham Parkway and City Island Road along Shore Road in the Borough of Bronx, New York.

As a project requiring FHWA approval, the Project is subject to the requirements of Section 4(f) of the USDOT Act of 1966 (now codified in 23 USC §138 and 49 USC §303), and the FHWA implementing regulation, 23 CFR Part 774. In accordance with the applicable regulations and as documented in the DEIS, the FHWA intends to make a de minimis impact finding for the Section 4(f) use of Pelham Bay Park and the Pelham Bay Park Preserve.  The FHWA is soliciting comments from the public on the proposed de minimis impact determination for Pelham Bay Park and the Pelham Bay Park Preserve.

Two in-person public hearings will be held to provide information and receive comments on the DDR/NEPA DEIS and SEQRA/CEQR documentation. The same content will be presented at both hearings.  One will be held on Thursday, October 1, 2026, from 6:00 p.m. to 8:00 pm at the Bartow Older Adult Center (Co-Op City) located at 2049 Bartow Avenue, Bronx, NY 10475 (Parking: Parking Garage 4, 99 Asch Loop, Bronx, NY 10475). The second will be held on Wednesday, October 7, 2026, from 6:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. at the Pelham Bay & Split Rock Golf Courses located at 870 Shore Road, Bronx, NY 10464 (parking available on site). Hearings will begin in an open-house format followed by a presentation and formal comment session for people who have signed up at the hearing to speak. Please submit any special accommodation requests by calling or emailing the contact below by 4:00 p.m., Monday, September 21, 2026. An on-demand presentation will also be available through the Project website after the completion of the in-person hearings.

 

Both the DDR/ NEPA DEIS and the SEQRA/CEQR Documentation are available at the Project website beginning September 4, 2026: https://www.nyc.gov/html/dot/html/infrastructure/shoreroadbridge.shtml

Digital and/or physical copies will be available at the following locations:

Pelham Bay Public Library: 3060 Middletown Road, Bronx, NY 10461;

Baychester Library: 2049 Asch Loop, Bronx, NY 10475; and

City Island Public Library: 320 City Island Avenue, Bronx, NY 10464.

Public comments on the SEQRA/CEQR Documentation, DDR/NEPA DEIS and the proposed Section 4(f) de minimis impact determination must be received by November 2, 2026.  Following the close of the public comment period, FHWA, NYSDOT and NYC DOT will review and consider comments received.

Contact: Joannene Kidder, NYC DOT, 55 Water Street, 5th Floor, New York, NY 10041, Phone: (929) 505-1002, E-mail: ShoreRoadBridgeBX@dot.nyc.gov

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that the following matters have been scheduled for public hearing by Community Board:

BOROUGH OF BROOKLYN

COMMUNITY BOARD NO. 7 Wednesday, September 30, 2026 6:00 p.m. Brooklyn Community 7 Office, 4201 4th Avenue (43rd Street entrance), Brooklyn, NY

 

AGENDA

The applicant, 783 4th Avenue LLC, is seeking zoning changes to facilitate a mixed-use development at 783 4th Avenue in Sunset Park. The proposed development would include three new buildings of 13, 9, and 8 stories, with 214 dwelling units, approximately 3,800 square feet of commercial space, 2,700 square feet of community facility space, and 9 parking spaces.

hearings.additional_description_1:
PLEASE TAKE NOTICE that a public hearing will be held on October 22, 2026 at the 224 West 124th Street Library, Manhattan, at 11:00 am, or as soon thereafter as the matter may be reached on the calendar, at which time and place those wishing to be heard will be given an opportunity to be heard concerning the proposed amendments to a deed and land disposition agreement identified below.

Pursuant to Section 695(2)(b) of the General Municipal Law and Section 1802(6)(j) of the Charter, the Department of Housing Preservation and Development ('HPD') of the City of New York ('City') proposed amendments to the terms and conditions of the sale of certain real property previously conveyed by the City of New York (collectively, 'Disposition Area') in the Borough of Manhattan:

 

              Address                      Block/Lots            Community District

              53 East 110 Street             1616/123             11

              304 East 126 Street           1802/47               11

              201 East 120 Street           1785/1                 11

              204 West 121 Street          1926/35               10

 

Under HPD's Division of Property Disposition and Finance program, City-owned vacant and/or occupied multifamily residential buildings may be purchased and gut-rehabilitated by a designated sponsor in order to create affordable rental housing units with a range of affordability. Construction and permanent financing is provided through loans from private institutional lenders and from public sources, including HPD.

On November 23, 2020, the City conveyed the Disposition Area to CLT East Harlem/El Barrio Community Land Trust Housing Development Fund Corporation. The deed and land disposition agreement recorded against the Premises requires compliance with a project summary approved by the Council requiring the development of approximately 36 rental dwelling units, two commercial spaces, and one community facility space. While it was originally intended that there would be commercial spaces in the project, it is now being developed with three community facility spaces and approximately 38 rental dwelling units. On July 16, 2026 (Res. No. 579), the Council approved and amended project summary reflecting these new conditions, and the deed and land disposition agreement will be amended to reflect these changes.                                                                                                      

A public file containing copies of the calendar document and other public documents will be made available to Manhattan Community Board 10 for public review at the office of Manhattan Community Board 10 no later than twenty (20) days prior to the public hearing.

The hearing location is accessible to individuals using wheelchairs or other mobility devices. For further information on accessibility or to make a request for accommodation, such as sign language interpretation services, please contact the Mayors Office of Contract Services (MOCS) via e-mail at disabilityaffairs@mocs.nyc.gov or via phone at (212) 788-0010. TDD users should call Verizon relay services.  Any person requiring reasonable accommodation for the public hearing should contact MOCS at least three (3) business days in advance of the hearing to ensure availability.

hearings.additional_description_1:
October 19th, 2026, and October 20th, 2026, 10:00 A.M. and 2:00 P.M.

 

      NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN of teleconference public hearings, Monday October 19th, 2026, at 10:00 A.M. and 2:00 P.M., and Tuesday October 20th, 2026, at 10:00 A.M. and 2:00 P.M., to be streamed live through the Boards website (www.nyc.gov/bsa), with remote public participation and in-person portion, on the following matters:

 

SPECIAL ORDER CALENDAR

80-54-BZIV

APPLICANT  Sheldon Lobel, P.C., for Dryden Hotel Associates, LLC, owner.

SUBJECT  Application August 24, 2026  Extension of Term (§11-411) of a previously granted variance which permitted commercial uses on the first floor and cellar of an existing residential building, which expired on July 26, 2026.  R8B zoning district.

PREMISES AFFECTED  150 East 39th Street, Block 894, Lot 52, Borough of Manhattan.

COMMUNITY BOARD #6M

 

182-85-BZIV

APPLICANT  Eric Palatnik, P.C., for Patsy Messina, owner.

SUBJECT  Application August 31, 2026  Extension of Term of a previously approved variance (§72-21) permitting the operation of a contractors establishment which expires on September 9, 2026, Extension of Time to Obtain a Certificate of Occupancy which expired on April 24, 2025; Waiver of the Boards Rules of Practice and Procedures.  R6B zoning district.   

PREMISES AFFECTED  209-211 20th Street, Block 637, Lot(s) 64, 65, Borough of Brooklyn.

COMMUNITY BOARD #7BK

 

183-85-BZIV

APPLICANT  Eric Palatnik, P.C., for Patsy Messina, owner.

SUBJECT  Application August 31, 2026   Extension of Term of a previously approved variance (§72-21) permitting the operation of a (UG 16) open storage yard for building materials and accessory parking for four cars with an accessory office and showroom which expires on September 9, 2026, Extension of Time to Obtain a Certificate of Occupancy which expired on April 24, 2025, Waiver of the Boards Rules of Practice and Procedures.  R6B zoning district.         

PREMISES AFFECTED  206-208 20th Street, Block 640, Lot 21, Borough of Brooklyn.

COMMUNITY BOARD #7BK

 

233-15-BZIII

APPLICANT  HSF Kramer, for ZDJ Vernon LLC, owner.

SUBJECT  Application June 29, 2026  Application to request an amendment to a previously approved variance granted pursuant to Zoning Resolution (ZR) § 72-21. The original variance permitted the conversion of a then-existing four-story manufacturing building and the development of a 21-story mixed retail and residential tower contrary to applicable district use and bulk regulations.  M1-6A/R9 zoning district.         

PREMISES AFFECTED  45-40 Vernon Boulevard, Block 26, Lot 4, Borough of Queens.

COMMUNITY BOARD #2Q

 

ZONING CALENDAR

2026-17-BZ

APPLICANT  Pryor Cashman LLP, for 25c LLC, owner.

SUBJECT  Application June 15, 2026    Special Permit (§73-44) to permit the reduction of required accessory off-street parking spaces for ambulatory diagnostic and treatment health care facility use (UG IIIB). M1-2 zoning district.         

PREMISES AFFECTED   27 & 25 Stewart Avenue, Block 2994, Lot 75, Borough of Brooklyn.

COMMUNITY BOARD #1BK

 

2026-28-BZ

APPLICANT  Eric Palatnik, P.C., for Peter Battisti, owner.

SUBJECT  Application July 20, 2026  Special Permits (§73-163 and §73-50) to permit the development of a Gasoline Service Station contrary to underlying use regulations and to waive the yard requirement for a lot line coincident with a side lot line of a residential district.  C2-3/R3-2 zoning district.      

PREMISES AFFECTED   254-11 Hillside Avenue, Block 8766, Lot  13, Borough of Queens.

COMMUNITY BOARD #13Q

 

Shampa Chanda, Chair/Commissioner

PLEASE TAKE NOTICE that a public hearing will be held on October 15, 2026 at the 9 West 124th Street at 11:00 am, or as soon thereafter as the matter may be reached on the calendar, at which time and place those wishing to be heard will be given an opportunity to be heard concerning the proposed amendments to a deed and land disposition agreement identified below.

 

Pursuant to Section 695(2)(b) of the General Municipal Law and Section 1802(6)(j) of the Charter, the Department of Housing Preservation and Development ('HPD') of the City of New York ('City') proposed amendments to the terms and conditions of the sale of certain real property previously conveyed by the City of New York (collectively, 'Disposition Area') in the Borough of Manhattan:

 

                Address                            Block/Lots         Community District

                53 East 110 Street            1616/123                  11

                304 East 126 Street           1802/47                    11

                201 East 120 Street           1785/1                      11

                204 West 121 Street          1926/35                    10

 

Under HPD's Division of Property Disposition and Finance program, City-owned vacant and/or occupied multifamily residential buildings may be purchased and gut-rehabilitated by a designated sponsor in order to create affordable rental housing units with a range of affordability. Construction and permanent financing is provided through loans from private institutional lenders and from public sources, including HPD.

 

On November 23, 2020, the City conveyed the Disposition Area to CLT East Harlem/El Barrio Community Land Trust Housing Development Fund Corporation. The deed and land disposition agreement recorded against the Premises requires compliance with a project summary approved by the Council requiring the development of approximately 36 rental dwelling units, two commercial spaces, and one community facility space. While it was originally intended that there would be commercial spaces in the project, it is now being developed with three community facility spaces and approximately 38 rental dwelling units. On July 16, 2026 (Res. No. 579), the Council approved and amended project summary reflecting these new conditions, and the deed and land disposition agreement will be amended to reflect these changes.

                                                                                                              

A public file containing copies of the calendar document and other public documents will be made available to Manhattan Community Board 10 for public review at the office of Manhattan Community Board 10 no later than twenty (20) days prior to the public hearing.

 

The hearing location is accessible to individuals using wheelchairs or other mobility devices. For further information on accessibility or to make a request for accommodation, such as sign language interpretation services, please contact the Mayors Office Of Contract Services (MOCS) via e-mail at disabilityaffairs@mocs.nyc.gov or via phone at (212) 788-0010.  TDD users should call Verizon relay services.  Any person requiring reasonable accommodation for the public hearing should contact MOCS at least three (3) business days in advance of the hearing to ensure availability.

Under HPD's Division of Property Disposition and Finance program, City-owned vacant and/or occupied multifamily residential buildings may be purchased and gut-rehabilitated by a designated sponsor in order to create affordable rental housing units with a range of affordability. Construction and permanent financing is provided through loans from private institutional lenders and from public sources, including HPD.

On November 23, 2020, the City conveyed the Disposition Area to CLT East Harlem/El Barrio Community Land Trust Housing Development Fund Corporation. The deed and land disposition agreement recorded against the Premises requires compliance with a project summary approved by the Council requiring the development of approximately 36 rental dwelling units, two commercial spaces, and one community facility space. While it was originally intended that there would be commercial spaces in the project, it is now being developed with three community facility spaces and approximately 38 rental dwelling units. On July 16, 2026 (Res. No. 579), the Council approved and amended project summary reflecting these new conditions, and the deed and land disposition agreement will be amended to reflect these changes.                                                                                                         

A public file containing copies of the calendar document and other public documents will be made available to Manhattan Community Board 10 for public review at the office of Manhattan Community Board 10 no later than twenty (20) days prior to the public hearing.

Pursuant to Section 695(2)(b) of the General Municipal Law and Section 1802(6)(j) of the Charter, the Department of Housing Preservation and Development ('HPD') of the City of New York ('City') has proposed the sale of the following City-owned property (collectively, 'Disposition Area') in the Borough of Brooklyn:

 

Address                                     Block/Lot(s)

435 Locke Street                        4445/ 50     

1050 Ashford Street                    4446/ 1     

1 Gateway Dr                              4445/ 1    (Formerly Block 4445, p/o Lot 1 and Block 4446, p/o Lot 1)

 

Under HPD's New Construction Finance Program, sponsors purchase City-owned or privately owned land or vacant buildings and construct multifamily buildings in order to create affordable rental housing.  Construction and permanent financing is provided through loans from private institutional lenders and from public sources including HPD, the New York City Housing Development Corporation, the State of New York, and the federal government. Additional funding may also be provided from the syndication of low-income housing tax credits. The newly constructed buildings provide rental housing affordable to low- and moderate-income households, with at least 60% of units affordable to households earning up to 80% of Area Median Income (AMI) and up to 40% of units affordable to households earning up to 120% of AMI. At least 15% of units are set aside for formerly homeless households.

 

Under the proposed project, the City will sell the Disposition Area to Nehemiah Spring Creek 5B Housing Development Fund Corporation ('Sponsor') for the nominal price of one dollar per tax lot. The Sponsor will also deliver an enforcement note and mortgage for the remainder of the appraised value (Land Debt). The Sponsor will then construct three buildings containing up to 200 rental dwelling units, including one superintendent unit, on the Disposition Area.

 

The Land Debt or the Citys capital subsidy may be repayable out of resale or refinancing profits for a period of at least thirty (30) years following completion of construction. The remaining balance, if any, may be forgiven at the end of the term.

 

The appraisal and the proposed Land Disposition Agreement and Project Summary are available for public examination by emailing Margaret Carey at careym@hpd.nyc.gov on business days during business hours.

hearings.additional_description_1:
NOTICE OF A JOINT PUBLIC HEARING of the Franchise and Concession Review Committee and Department of Transportation (DOT) to be held on 10/13/2026, at 255 Greenwich Street, 8th Floor, New York, NY 10007 commencing at 2:30pm relative to:

INTENT TO AWARD as a concession a License Agreement (License) to Summerville Enterprises, Inc. (Concessionaire) for the development, operation, and maintenance of a food, beverage, and/or merchandise concession at Café Building and Kiosk 2, Fordham Plaza, the Bronx.

The License provides for one (1) ten (10)-year term, commencing upon written Notice to Proceed, which may be renewed for up to two (2) additional five (5)-year terms, exercisable at the sole discretion of DOT.

Compensation to the City will be as follows: The Concessionaire will be required to invest any revenue generated by this concession into the maintenance and/or repair of the Licensed Premises.

Written testimony may be submitted in advance of the hearing electronically to fcrc@mocs.nyc.gov. All written testimony can be submitted up until the close of the public hearing and will be distributed to the FCRC after the hearing.

A draft copy of the agreement may be obtained at no cost by any (or all) of the
following ways:

  1. Submit a written request to DOT at concessions@dot.nyc.gov from 9/28/2026 through 10/13/2026.
  2. Submit a written request by mail to Department of Transportation, 55 Water Street, 9th Floor, New York, NY 10038. Written requests must be received by 12/1/2025. For mail-in requests, please include your name, return address, and Summerville Enterprises, Inc. Concession/2025Con01.

The agenda for the hearing will be posted on the MOCS website at https://www.nyc.gov/site/mocs/opportunities/franchises-concessions.page

For further information on accessibility or to make a request for accommodations, such as sign language interpretation services, please contact the Mayors Office of Contract Services (MOCS) via e-mail at DisabilityAffairs@mocs.nyc.gov or via phone at (212) 298-0800. Any person requiring reasonable accommodation for the public hearing should contact MOCS at least five (5) business days in advance of the hearing to ensure availability.

hearings.additional_description_1:
COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT PROGRAM - DISASTER RECOVERY

PUBLIC NOTICE OF AVAILABILITY

NOTICE OF A PUBLIC HEARING

 

TO ALL INTERESTED RESIDENTS, GROUPS, COMMUNITY BOARDS, AND AGENCIES:

On Monday, September 14, 2026, the City of New York will release a substantial amendment to its Community Development Block Grant-Disaster Recovery (CDBG-DR) Action Plan for Hurricane Ida Recovery. Through this amendment, the City will detail its proposed use of $86,000,000 in reallocated CDBG-DR funding provided through the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD).

To access the plan beginning September 14, 2026, please visit: https://www.nyc.gov/site/cdbgdr/hurricane-ida/ida-action-plan.page. Executive Summaries will be available in English, Spanish, Chinese, Russian, Bengali, Haitian, Korean, Arabic, Urdu, French, and Polish. The online materials will also be accessible for the visually impaired. Paper copies of the Action Plan, including in large print format (18pt. font size), will be provided upon request.

The substantial amendment is subject to a 30-day public comment period, which will begin on September 15, 2026. Comments must be received no later than Friday, October 16, 2026 at 11:59 P.M. (EST). Written comments may be submitted to CDBGComments@omb.nyc.gov or to the Mayors Office of Management and Budget (OMB), Attention: Evan Pellegrino, Director of Community Development, 255 Greenwich Street, 8th Floor, New York, New York 10007.

A hearing is scheduled for October 8, 2026 from 6:00-7:00pm to obtain comments on the City's use of federal funds. The hearing may be attended either in person or virtually. Information for attending the hearing virtually or in person is below:

ZOOM link for virtual participation:

https://us06web.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_fK1Fx3ylR5OpGKLrWtmhBA

Webinar ID: 897 3335 4124

Passcode: 1

Location for in person participation:

NYC City Planning Commission Hearing Room

120 Broadway, Lower Concourse

New York, New York 10002 

 

Please inform NYC Department of City Planning if you need reasonable accommodation or foreign language interpretation services, such as but not limited to sign language interpretation, to participate in the public hearing. Foreign language interpretation will be provided based on available resources. Please email requests to accessibilityinfo@planning.nyc.gov or call 212-720-3366 at least five business days before the hearing.

 

At the end of the comment period, all comments shall be reviewed, and City responses will be incorporated into the final Action Plan. The final Ida Action Plan, containing a summary of the comments and the City's responses, will be submitted to HUD and posted on the City's CDBG-DR website.

 

City of New York:      Zohran Kwame Mamdani, Mayor

                                    Sherif Soliman, Director, Mayors Office of Management and Budget

Date: September 11, 2026

Through this amendment, the City will detail its proposed use of $86,000,000 in reallocated CDBG-DR funding provided through the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD).

To access the plan beginning September 14, 2026, please visit: https://www.nyc.gov/site/cdbgdr/hurricane-ida/ida-action-plan.page. Executive Summaries will be available in English, Spanish, Chinese, Russian, Bengali, Haitian, Korean, Arabic, Urdu, French, and Polish. The online materials will also be accessible for the visually impaired. Paper copies of the Action Plan, including in large print format (18pt. font size), will be provided upon request.

The substantial amendment is subject to a 30-day public comment period, which will begin on September 15, 2026. Comments must be received no later than Friday, October 16, 2026 at 11:59 P.M. (EST). Written comments may be submitted to CDBGComments@omb.nyc.gov or to the Mayors Office of Management and Budget (OMB), Attention: Evan Pellegrino, Director of Community Development, 255 Greenwich Street, 8th Floor, New York, New York 10007.

A hearing is scheduled for October 8, 2026 from 6:00-7:00pm to obtain comments on the City's use of federal funds. The hearing may be attended either in person or virtually. Information for attending the hearing virtually or in person is below:

ZOOM link for virtual participation:

https://us06web.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_fK1Fx3ylR5OpGKLrWtmhBA

Webinar ID: 897 3335 4124

Passcode: 1

Location for in person participation:

NYC City Planning Commission Hearing Room

120 Broadway, Lower Concourse

New York, New York 10002

Please inform NYC Department of City Planning if you need reasonable accommodation or foreign language interpretation services, such as but not limited to sign language interpretation, to participate in the public hearing. Foreign language interpretation will be provided based on available resources. Please email requests to accessibilityinfo@planning.nyc.gov or call 212-720-3366 at least five business days before the hearing.

At the end of the comment period, all comments shall be reviewed, and City responses will be incorporated into the final Action Plan. The final Ida Action Plan, containing a summary of the comments and the City's responses, will be submitted to HUD and posted on the City's CDBG-DR website.

City of New York: Zohran Kwame Mamdani, Mayor

Sherif Soliman, Director, Mayors Office of Management and Budget

Date: September 11, 2026

hearings.short_title: Shore Road Bridge over Hutchinson River Project
hearings.street_address_1: Address Not Listed In The Dropdown
hearings.additional_description_1:
Bronx County (Bronx) - The Federal Highway Administration (FHWA), the New York State Department of Transportation (NYSDOT), as joint lead agencies, and the New York City Department of Transportation (NYC DOT), as project sponsor and joint lead agency, have made available the Draft Design Report (DDR) / NEPA Draft Environmental Impact Statement (DEIS) for the Shore Road Bridge over the Hutchinson River Project. In compliance with SEQRA/CEQR, the NYC DOT has also prepared additional documentation to cover topics not addressed in the DDR/NEPA DEIS.

The purpose of the Project is to address the structural deficiencies; geometric deficiencies; and operational reliability for multi-modal users, including marine vessels, of the Shore Road Bridge over the Hutchinson River. The existing Shore Road Bridge is over 115 years old and is an 865-foot-long bridge with seven spans. The main span over the navigation channel is a double-leaf movable bascule span, which opens for the passage of marine vessels. The bridge is located within Pelham Bay Park between the Bronx and Pelham Parkway and City Island Road along Shore Road in the Borough of Bronx, New York.

As a project requiring FHWA approval, the Project is subject to the requirements of Section 4(f) of the USDOT Act of 1966 (now codified in 23 USC §138 and 49 USC §303), and the FHWA implementing regulation, 23 CFR Part 774. In accordance with the applicable regulations and as documented in the DEIS, the FHWA intends to make a de minimis impact finding for the Section 4(f) use of Pelham Bay Park and the Pelham Bay Park Preserve.  The FHWA is soliciting comments from the public on the proposed de minimis impact determination for Pelham Bay Park and the Pelham Bay Park Preserve.

Two in-person public hearings will be held to provide information and receive comments on the DDR/NEPA DEIS and SEQRA/CEQR documentation. The same content will be presented at both hearings.  One will be held on Thursday, October 1, 2026, from 6:00 p.m. to 8:00 pm at the Bartow Older Adult Center (Co-Op City) located at 2049 Bartow Avenue, Bronx, NY 10475 (Parking: Parking Garage 4, 99 Asch Loop, Bronx, NY 10475). The second will be held on Wednesday, October 7, 2026, from 6:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. at the Pelham Bay & Split Rock Golf Courses located at 870 Shore Road, Bronx, NY 10464 (parking available on site). Hearings will begin in an open-house format followed by a presentation and formal comment session for people who have signed up at the hearing to speak. Please submit any special accommodation requests by calling or emailing the contact below by 4:00 p.m., Monday, September 21, 2026. An on-demand presentation will also be available through the Project website after the completion of the in-person hearings.

 

Both the DDR/ NEPA DEIS and the SEQRA/CEQR Documentation are available at the Project website beginning September 4, 2026: https://www.nyc.gov/html/dot/html/infrastructure/shoreroadbridge.shtml

Digital and/or physical copies will be available at the following locations:

Pelham Bay Public Library: 3060 Middletown Road, Bronx, NY 10461;

Baychester Library: 2049 Asch Loop, Bronx, NY 10475; and

City Island Public Library: 320 City Island Avenue, Bronx, NY 10464.

Public comments on the SEQRA/CEQR Documentation, DDR/NEPA DEIS and the proposed Section 4(f) de minimis impact determination must be received by November 2, 2026.  Following the close of the public comment period, FHWA, NYSDOT and NYC DOT will review and consider comments received.

Contact: Joannene Kidder, NYC DOT, 55 Water Street, 5th Floor, New York, NY 10041, Phone: (929) 505-1002, E-mail: ShoreRoadBridgeBX@dot.nyc.gov

hearings.short_title: Shore Road Bridge over Hutchinson River Project
hearings.street_address_1: Address Not Listed In The Dropdown
hearings.additional_description_1:
Bronx County (Bronx) - The Federal Highway Administration (FHWA), the New York State Department of Transportation (NYSDOT), as joint lead agencies, and the New York City Department of Transportation (NYC DOT), as project sponsor and joint lead agency, have made available the Draft Design Report (DDR) / NEPA Draft Environmental Impact Statement (DEIS) for the Shore Road Bridge over the Hutchinson River Project. In compliance with SEQRA/CEQR, the NYC DOT has also prepared additional documentation to cover topics not addressed in the DDR/NEPA DEIS.

The purpose of the Project is to address the structural deficiencies; geometric deficiencies; and operational reliability for multi-modal users, including marine vessels, of the Shore Road Bridge over the Hutchinson River. The existing Shore Road Bridge is over 115 years old and is an 865-foot-long bridge with seven spans. The main span over the navigation channel is a double-leaf movable bascule span, which opens for the passage of marine vessels. The bridge is located within Pelham Bay Park between the Bronx and Pelham Parkway and City Island Road along Shore Road in the Borough of Bronx, New York.

As a project requiring FHWA approval, the Project is subject to the requirements of Section 4(f) of the USDOT Act of 1966 (now codified in 23 USC §138 and 49 USC §303), and the FHWA implementing regulation, 23 CFR Part 774. In accordance with the applicable regulations and as documented in the DEIS, the FHWA intends to make a de minimis impact finding for the Section 4(f) use of Pelham Bay Park and the Pelham Bay Park Preserve.  The FHWA is soliciting comments from the public on the proposed de minimis impact determination for Pelham Bay Park and the Pelham Bay Park Preserve.

Two in-person public hearings will be held to provide information and receive comments on the DDR/NEPA DEIS and SEQRA/CEQR documentation. The same content will be presented at both hearings.  One will be held on Thursday, October 1, 2026, from 6:00 p.m. to 8:00 pm at the Bartow Older Adult Center (Co-Op City) located at 2049 Bartow Avenue, Bronx, NY 10475 (Parking: Parking Garage 4, 99 Asch Loop, Bronx, NY 10475). The second will be held on Wednesday, October 7, 2026, from 6:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. at the Pelham Bay & Split Rock Golf Courses located at 870 Shore Road, Bronx, NY 10464 (parking available on site). Hearings will begin in an open-house format followed by a presentation and formal comment session for people who have signed up at the hearing to speak. Please submit any special accommodation requests by calling or emailing the contact below by 4:00 p.m., Monday, September 21, 2026. An on-demand presentation will also be available through the Project website after the completion of the in-person hearings.

 

Both the DDR/ NEPA DEIS and the SEQRA/CEQR Documentation are available at the Project website beginning September 4, 2026: https://www.nyc.gov/html/dot/html/infrastructure/shoreroadbridge.shtml

Digital and/or physical copies will be available at the following locations:

Pelham Bay Public Library: 3060 Middletown Road, Bronx, NY 10461;

City Island Public Library: 320 City Island Avenue, Bronx, NY 10464.

Public comments on the SEQRA/CEQR Documentation, DDR/NEPA DEIS and the proposed Section 4(f) de minimis impact determination must be received by November 2, 2026.  Following the close of the public comment period, FHWA, NYSDOT and NYC DOT will review and consider comments received.
